Compute Krippendorff's alpha across raters

Source: R/api-krippendorff-alpha.R, R/api-pairwise-icc.R, R/api-tables.R, and 1 more
interrater_agreement_table.Rd

Estimate observed-score agreement across two or more raters, allowing unequal numbers of ratings per unit. This is Krippendorff's agreement coefficient, not Cronbach's internal-consistency alpha or MFRM separation reliability. No measurement-model fitting is performed.

Compare each pair on its common, complete units using a two-way ANOVA ICC. No MFRM fit, mixed-model estimation or extra package is required.

Compare observed scores on matched units for every pair of raters, using quadratic (QWK), linear or unweighted agreement. No model is fitted.

Compute observed-score agreement across two or more raters, with a declared category universe and quadratic, linear or unweighted agreement.

Usage

krippendorff_alpha_table(
  data,
  rater,
  unit,
  score,
  level = c("nominal", "ordinal", "interval", "ratio"),
  categories = NULL
)

pairwise_icc_table(
  data,
  rater,
  unit,
  score,
  model = c("mixed", "random"),
  definition = c("agreement", "consistency"),
  type = c("single", "average")
)

interrater_agreement_table(
  fit,
  diagnostics = NULL,
  rater_facet = NULL,
  context_facets = NULL,
  exact_warn = 0.5,
  corr_warn = 0.3,
  include_precision = TRUE,
  top_n = NULL
)

pairwise_kappa_table(
  data,
  rater,
  unit,
  score,
  categories,
  weights = c("quadratic", "linear", "unweighted")
)

gwet_ac2_table(
  data,
  rater,
  unit,
  score,
  categories,
  weights = c("quadratic", "linear", "unweighted")
)

Arguments

data

Long-format ratings with at most one row per rater and unit.

rater

Name of the rater identifier column.

unit

Names of columns jointly identifying a rated unit, such as c("Person", "Task").

score

Name of the score column. Values may be numeric, character, factor or logical, with NA for missing scores. Factors use their labels.

level

Measurement level: "nominal" (default), "ordinal", "interval" or "ratio". Choose on substantive grounds; numeric category codes alone do not establish an interval or ratio scale.

categories

Required distinct permitted category values, including unused categories, in their substantive order. At least two are required. They must have the same numeric/character/logical representation as scores. With linear/quadratic weights, numeric values use their actual spacing; character/logical values use equally spaced positions in this vector. Factor levels never silently determine the order. To treat numeric codes as equally spaced ranks, explicitly convert scores and categories to character. Choose spacing on substantive grounds.

model

"mixed" (default) describes the selected raters. "random" assumes raters were sampled from a population to which results may generalize. Two-way point formulas are identical; their interpretation differs. Choosing "random" does not establish random sampling.

definition

"agreement" (default) includes systematic rater offsets; "consistency" removes their contribution.

type

"single" (default) concerns one rating; "average" concerns the unweighted mean of the two ratings, not a mean over the full panel.

fit

Output from fit_mfrm().

diagnostics

Optional output from diagnose_mfrm().

rater_facet

Name of the rater facet. If NULL, inferred from facet names.

context_facets

Optional context facets used to match observations for agreement. If NULL, all remaining facets (including Person) are used.

exact_warn

Warning threshold for exact agreement.

corr_warn

Warning threshold for pairwise correlation.

include_precision

If TRUE, append rater severity spread indices from the facet precision summary when available.

top_n

Optional maximum number of pair rows to keep, after ordering by flag, exact agreement and correlation. The summary still describes all candidate pairs. Leave NULL to retain the complete pair audit.

weights

One of "quadratic" (default), "linear" or "unweighted". Agreement weights are 1 minus squared normalized distance, 1 minus normalized absolute distance, or the identity matrix, respectively.

Value

A plain list with table (alpha, observed/expected disagreement, availability and sample counts), counts (category values, nonmissing and pairable counts, plus ordinal positions), cases (input rows and exclusion reasons), unit_summary (assignment counts and unit disagreements), units (unique input unit keys), settings and notes. Unit indexes rows of units. Save with base::saveRDS(); export data frames with utils::write.csv(). Reopening the saved list performs no calculation.

A plain list containing table (one row per rater pair), anova (scaled ANOVA ingredients), cases (one row per pair and union of assigned units, with input-row references and inclusion flags), units (the unique input unit keys in input-column order), settings and notes. Unit in cases is a row index into units. Units assigned to neither member of a pair are outside that pair's audit. Missing1/Missing2 indicate explicit missing-score rows; Assigned1/Assigned2 also distinguish absent assignments. Save with base::saveRDS() and export data frames with utils::write.csv(). Reading saved output performs no calculation.

An mfrm_interrater bundle (a named list) with:

  • summary: one-row inter-rater summary

  • pairs: pair-level agreement table

  • notes: interpretation and availability qualifications

  • settings: applied options and thresholds

Use summary(ir) or ir$summary to inspect a result and plot(ir) for its saved agreement figure. Save the full bundle with base::saveRDS() and reopen with base::readRDS(); export ir$pairs and ir$summary separately with utils::write.csv(). Reopening performs no fitting. plot(ir, type = "agreement", metric = "correlation") selects the correlation view; metric = "difference" selects observed-score gaps. These plots retain the saved flag thresholds. Changing them requires recreating this result from the existing fit, not fitting a new model. as_ggplot() converts a saved plot payload without recomputation.

A plain list with table (one row per pair), counts (nonzero retained contingency cells, with category indices), categories (indices, values and weighting positions), weights (agreement matrix), cases, units, settings and notes. Unit indexes units. Save with base::saveRDS() or export data frames with utils::write.csv().

A plain list with table (coefficient, observed/expected agreement, status and counts), counts (category totals and unit-mean proportions), categories, weights, cases (input rows and their two inclusion flags), unit_summary, units, settings and notes. Unit indexes units. Results can be saved with base::saveRDS() without refitting on reload.

Details

The coefficient is \(1-D_o/D_e\). Only units with at least two nonmissing scores contribute to either disagreement. A unit with m ratings contributes its ordered rating pairs divided by m-1 to the coincidence counts, hence contributes m pairable ratings overall. Units are not equally weighted when m differs. The expected disagreement draws two distinct observations without replacement from the pooled pairable ratings, with denominator n(n-1), where n is the number of pairable ratings. This is not Cohen's kappa chance model or MFRM model-implied expected agreement.

The squared difference function is 0/1 mismatch for nominal scores, frequency-based rank distance for ordinal scores, squared numeric difference for interval scores, and \(((c-k)/(c+k))^2\) for ratio scores (0 when both values are zero). Ordinal positions use cumulative pairable-category counts minus half the category count, divided by n. The squared difference between these positions is proportional to Krippendorff's ordinal distance. It is not quadratic weighting of category numbers or equally spaced category ranks. Unused ranks and singleton-only categories do not alter pairable distances.

Interval distances are calculated after subtracting score_offset, dividing by score_half_range, and dividing by 2, using only pairable values to set the offset and half-range. Constant pairable values map to zero. This avoids squaring very large or tiny raw scores. The common normalization leaves alpha unchanged; reported disagreements are on this normalized scale, not original squared score units. Ordinal positions are similarly normalized by n. Nominal and ratio disagreements use their stated distance directly. Computation avoids a dense category-by-category matrix. Ratio computation still requires quadratic time in the number of distinct pairable values.

No rows are imputed and repeated rater-unit cells are rejected, including repetitions with missing scores. All input rows remain in cases. unit_summary distinguishes missing scores on assigned rows from absent assignments relative to the observed rater roster. Units with no input rows at all are unknown to the function. Missingness and selective assignment may affect representativeness; numerical handling does not correct that bias.

Negative estimates are retained. With no pairable ratings or zero expected disagreement, alpha is unavailable with a reason rather than set to 0 or 1. A finite coefficient describes this pooled rating sample, not each rater's accuracy against a reference or a guarantee of interchangeable ratings. There are no confidence intervals, tests, quality cutoffs or bootstrap claims. Dependencies among several tasks from one person require attention in any subsequent sampling inference. Circular, bipolar and custom metrics are not implemented.

All observed rater identifiers are paired. Each pair uses only units with two nonmissing scores. Other raters' missing scores do not exclude a unit for that pair. Missing-score rows and absent assignments are distinguished in cases. Duplicate rater-unit cells (including missing-score duplicates) are rejected rather than averaged. Identifiers must be nonmissing and nonblank. There is no imputation or observation weighting. Pairs with fewer than two complete units remain in table with an unavailable ICC.

Let R, C and E be the unit, rater and residual ANOVA mean squares on a complete n-by-2 matrix. Following Koo and Li (2016, Table 3), the numerator is R-E. The single-rating denominator is R+E for consistency, or R+E+2(C-E)/n for absolute agreement. The average-rating denominator is R for consistency, or R+(C-E)/n for agreement. Form records ICC(C,1), ICC(A,1), ICC(C,2) or ICC(A,2); interpret these together with Model. ICC(A,2) denotes an average of two ratings, not Shrout–Fleiss ICC(2,1). One-way ICCs are not computed.

Negative estimates are retained. A nonpositive denominator makes ICC unavailable and sets Status = "nonpositive_denominator"; RawICC retains the algebraic ratio when finite so it cannot masquerade as a valid reliability estimate. An entirely constant matrix is undefined, not 1. Internally scores are shifted and scaled to avoid overflow/underflow. anova records scaled mean squares, the offset/scale, numerator and denominator, so the calculation can be reconstructed. These scaled mean squares are not variances in the original score units.

Results describe each pair's retained unit mix. Different pairs can have different units and score ranges; their ICCs cannot automatically rank rater quality and should not be averaged into a panel ICC. Restricted unit variability can lower ICC without larger absolute disagreement. Inference requires a suitable sampling design and assumptions about errors and dependence. Treating several tasks from one person as separate units does not make them independent. No confidence intervals, hypothesis tests, quality bands or rater-training decisions are supplied. This is distinct from the component variance shares in compute_facet_icc(), MFRM separation reliability and the fitted expected agreement in interrater_agreement_table().

Computes pairwise rater agreement on matched contexts (pairs and one-row summary). Model-implied expected exact agreement is \(\sum_k P_{r1}(X=k)P_{r2}(X=k)\) evaluated conditionally at saved Person point estimates (including MML EAPs) and structural parameters, without posterior integration or calibration-uncertainty propagation. Nonfinite primary estimates, repeated rater-context cells (whose observed scores are weight-averaged), or unavailable GPCM slopes set ExpectedExact = NA with explicit ExpectedReason (primary_estimate_unavailable, repeated_ratings, fitted_probabilities_unavailable, or no_matched_scores).

Each matched context with two finite scores contributes one opportunity per rater pair (\(m\) judges on one context contribute \(m(m-1)/2\) opportunities). Exact, Adjacent (\(|d| \le 1\)), MeanDiff (Rater1 - Rater2), MAD, and Corr summarize matched pairs; MeanCorr weights pairwise correlations by N. Flag marks configured exact_warn / corr_warn thresholds (FlaggedShare = NA when classification is incomplete). For two-way ICCs, kappa, AC2, or Krippendorff's alpha without an MFRM fit, see pairwise_icc_table() and mfrmr_methods_reference.

For each pair, both observed and expected agreement use only common complete units. Expected cell proportions are products of the two rater-specific margins on this same sample. Kappa is (observed - expected)/(1 - expected). This complete-case convention differs from the all-available rater margins in Gwet's incomplete-data Example 4.1. Different pairs may retain different cohorts; comparing or averaging their kappas does not establish a panel coefficient. At least two complete units are required, as in the existing QWK score-comparison interface.

Computation uses the equivalent disagreement ratio, with distances rescaled to the categories actually present in each retained pair. The common scale cancels, avoiding loss of the coefficient when an unused numeric category is very distant. ScaledObservedDisagreement and ScaledExpectedDisagreement retain those ingredients; agreement columns use the declared full-scale weights. Agreement columns can round to 1 at extreme relative spacings even when kappa is defined. Negative estimates remain visible; zero expected disagreement returns NA with a status.

Duplicate rater-unit cells are rejected before dropping missing scores. The case audit distinguishes an absent assignment from an explicit missing score and retains the union of units assigned to either member of the pair. No imputation, confidence intervals, tests or quality cutoffs are supplied. Missingness may affect representativeness. Agreement does not establish reference accuracy or MFRM rater-severity homogeneity. Storage of the weight matrix requires space quadratic in the number of declared categories; these are categorical-score interfaces, not continuous-score ICCs.

Observed agreement is the equally weighted mean of within-unit weighted agreement over distinct ordered rating pairs, using only units with at least two nonmissing ratings. Category proportions are the equally weighted mean of within-unit category proportions over all units with at least one rating. Thus singletons contribute to expected agreement but not observed agreement; units with no ratings contribute to neither. This is Gwet's raw-rating convention, not Krippendorff's pairable-rating margins or Cohen's separate rater margins. Unequal rating counts do not give units greater weight.

With q declared categories, agreement matrix W and mean category proportions pi, expected agreement is sum(W) * sum(pi * (1 - pi)) / (q * (q - 1)). AC is (observed - expected)/(1 - expected). Quadratic/linear weights give AC2; identity weights give AC1. At two categories the supplied linear and quadratic weights equal identity weights, so the numerical results coincide. The complete category universe is required: adding unused categories can change expected agreement and AC. It must not be selected to improve a result.

Negative estimates are retained. No pairable units or a nonpositive chance denominator gives NA with a status. With all raters always using the same category, AC can be 1 when the declared universe has at least two categories; this does not establish discrimination, validity or reference accuracy. Unlike kappa, its chance model does not become undefined in that case.

Repeated rater-unit cells are rejected, even when scores are missing. Audits distinguish explicit missing scores from absent assignments relative to the observed rater roster. Units with no input rows are unknown. Missingness and assignment may still bias interpretation. Results are descriptive point estimates: no confidence intervals, tests, quality bands or invariance to prevalence are claimed. Different chance models answer different questions; AC2 is not an automatic replacement or correction for kappa. Dense weight storage is quadratic in the declared category count. Custom weights and circular, bipolar, radical and ratio weights are not implemented.

References

Krippendorff, K. (2011; literature updated 2013). Computing Krippendorff's Alpha-Reliability. Sections A-E, pp. 1-10. https://www.asc.upenn.edu/krippendorffs-alpha-reliability

Koo, T. K., & Li, M. Y. (2016). A guideline of selecting and reporting intraclass correlation coefficients for reliability research. Journal of Chiropractic Medicine, 15(2), 155-163. doi:10.1016/j.jcm.2016.02.012 . Table 3; see also the 2017 erratum, doi:10.1016/j.jcm.2017.10.001 , correcting the one-way ICC(1,1) formula.

Cohen, J. (1968). Weighted kappa: nominal scale agreement with provision for scaled disagreement or partial credit. Psychological Bulletin, 70, 213-220. doi:10.1037/h0026256 .

Gwet, K. L. Handbook of Inter-Rater Reliability, fifth edition, volume 1, chapter 4, pp. 100-110, equations 4.2.4-4.2.6. https://www.agreestat.com/assets/cac5-chapter4-excerpt.pdf

Gwet, K. L. Author implementation of AC1/AC2, gwet.ac1.raw, and linear/quadratic weights, in irrCAC. https://github.com/kgwet/irrCAC/blob/master/R/agree.coeff3.raw.r https://github.com/kgwet/irrCAC/blob/master/R/weights.gen.r

Examples

data("mfrmr_example_agreement", package = "mfrmr")
ratings <- mfrmr_example_agreement
agreement <- krippendorff_alpha_table(ratings, rater = "Rater",
  unit = c("Person", "Task"), score = "Score", level = "ordinal", categories = 0:3)
agreement$table
#>       Alpha   Level    Status ObservedDisagreement ExpectedDisagreement Raters
#> 1 0.5666233 ordinal available           0.06785569            0.1565744      3
#>   Units PairableUnits PairableRatings NonmissingRatings MissingScores
#> 1    12            12              34                34             1
#>   SingletonUnits UnratedUnits
#> 1              0            0
agreement$unit_summary # Each response needs at least two observed ratings.
#>    Unit AssignedRows NonmissingRatings MissingScores AbsentAssignments Included
#> 1     1            3                 3             0                 0     TRUE
#> 2     2            3                 3             0                 0     TRUE
#> 3     3            3                 3             0                 0     TRUE
#> 4     4            2                 2             0                 1     TRUE
#> 5     5            3                 3             0                 0     TRUE
#> 6     6            3                 3             0                 0     TRUE
#> 7     7            3                 3             0                 0     TRUE
#> 8     8            3                 3             0                 0     TRUE
#> 9     9            3                 3             0                 0     TRUE
#> 10   10            3                 3             0                 0     TRUE
#> 11   11            3                 3             0                 0     TRUE
#> 12   12            3                 2             1                 0     TRUE
#>    ObservedDisagreement
#> 1            0.05204729
#> 2            0.07626874
#> 3            0.15844867
#> 4            0.07807093
#> 5            0.07626874
#> 6            0.03243945
#> 7            0.05204729
#> 8            0.07626874
#> 9            0.03243945
#> 10           0.05204729
#> 11           0.07626874
#> 12           0.04865917
agreement$notes
#> [1] "Krippendorff's alpha measures pooled observed-score agreement, not Cronbach's alpha, MFRM separation reliability or criterion-referenced rater accuracy."
#> [2] "Only pairable ratings contribute to observed and expected disagreement; unequal rating counts weight units differently."                                 
#> [3] "Missingness and selective assignment may affect representativeness; no imputation or automatic correction is made."                                      
#> [4] "No confidence intervals, tests or quality cutoffs are supplied; negative estimates are retained."

# Ordinal alpha uses category ordering; it is not quadratic weighted kappa.
# Optional workflow; run the example explicitly as shown below.
# example("pairwise_icc_table", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
data("mfrmr_example_agreement", package = "mfrmr")
ratings <- mfrmr_example_agreement
absolute <- pairwise_icc_table(ratings, rater = "Rater",
  unit = c("Person", "Task"), score = "Score", definition = "agreement")
consistent <- pairwise_icc_table(ratings, rater = "Rater",
  unit = c("Person", "Task"), score = "Score", definition = "consistency")
absolute$table
consistent$table
# R1/R2 have perfect consistency, but R2's one-category offset reduces agreement.
# These ICCs treat 0--3 as numeric scores; justify equal score intervals.
} # }
# Optional workflow; run the example explicitly as shown below.
# example("interrater_agreement_table", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(mfrmr)

# Saved synthetic MML/RSM analysis of example_operational.
# For your own data, fit a model first; see ?fit_mfrm.
example_fit <- readRDS(system.file("examples", "operational-mml.rds", package = "mfrmr"))
fit <- example_fit$fit

# Compare ratings of the same person on the same criterion
agreement <- interrater_agreement_table(fit, rater_facet = "Rater")
agreement$summary
agreement$pairs[, c("Rater1", "Rater2", "N", "Exact", "Corr", "MeanDiff")]
# N is the number of matched ratings; Exact is the fraction with identical scores
# MeanDiff = Rater1 minus Rater2: positive means Rater1 assigned higher scores
# These observed-score comparisons are distinct from fitted rater severity
} # }
# Optional workflow; run the example explicitly as shown below.
# example("pairwise_kappa_table", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
data("mfrmr_example_agreement", package = "mfrmr")
ratings <- mfrmr_example_agreement
head(ratings) # One rater's score for one Person-Task response.
pairs <- pairwise_kappa_table(ratings, rater = "Rater",
  unit = c("Person", "Task"), score = "Score", categories = 0:3)
pairs$table
pairs$cases # Included marks the shared nonmissing ratings for each pair.
# R2 gives every response one category more than R1: equal rankings do not
# imply agreement. Do not treat two Tasks by the same Person as one response.
} # }
# Optional workflow; run the example explicitly as shown below.
# example("gwet_ac2_table", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
data("mfrmr_example_agreement", package = "mfrmr")
ratings <- mfrmr_example_agreement
ac <- gwet_ac2_table(ratings, rater = "Rater",
  unit = c("Person", "Task"), score = "Score", categories = 0:3)
ac$table
ac$unit_summary # Number of observed ratings and pairability for each response.
ac$notes # Read the panel coefficient together with its assumptions.
} # }
